column1: # Every problem, every run. Appended, never pruned. One row per problem.
# Columns: date | phase | source | what happened | severity | resolved
#   source    the podcast, newsletter, vendor, report publisher, or script involved. "-" if none.
#   severity  blocked (stopped the run), degraded (ran, but something is missing), noted (worth watching)
#   resolved  yes if it fixed itself or was worked around this run, no if it is still outstanding
# Anything appearing three times stops being a hiccup. Fix it properly in the
# code, or write it into TROUBLESHOOTING.md as a known problem with a known
# workaround. See the review rule there.
# Count how often a source has caused trouble:
#   grep -v "^#" RUN_LOG.tsv | cut -f3 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

Flagged the GPT-6 Astra pricing bullet ($10/$50 per million tokens) as a "market figure with no market named". Reviewed: this is global API pricing, not country-specific labour-market data, so a market label would misstate it. Left as-is.

Digest guest line and Standout row read "Cait Malinsson". The library file (library/podcasts/transcripts/PromptMates/2026-09-10-ai-talent-operations-at-elevenlabs.md) never states a surname: the transcript renders it "Kate" (auto-caption) and the episode description gives only "Cait". The only surname in the file is in the helper-written summary block, which is not evidence per TOKEN_RULES section 8. A web search returned "Cait Mallinson - ElevenLabs" (LinkedIn /in/caitlin-mallinson-1919edinb/), a different spelling. MISMATCH - builder must confirm spelling from a first-party source.

Item displayed as 10 Sep 2026, matching the library file's Date field, but that is one day AFTER the 8 week window ending Wednesday 9 September 2026 and after the edition date itself. The PromptMates Newsletter of 2026-09-08 lists this session as "Wednesday, September 9", so 2026-09-10 looks like the YouTube publish date rather than the episode date. MISMATCH - fix the library date or drop the item.

Bullet 2 quotes vague "I'm kind of a three" feedback. That exact string is not in the transcript. Source (13:26) says "...and like this I'm kind of neutral on. So I I guess I'm a three." Two separate phrases welded into one quotation. MISMATCH - quote "I guess I'm a three" or drop the quote marks.

Bullet 1 says Yan says companies "overhired" during the low-rate years. "Low-rate" appears nowhere in the transcript. Yan (11:51) says only "they overhired for various reasons"; the only period named is the host's "the covid era" (1:39), and that is the host, not Yan. MISMATCH - drop the qualifier or attribute it to the host.

Bullet 1 says this year's real obligations are "just the AI ban and the August transparency duty". Source (28:33-29:18) names three live obligation sets before Dec 2027: prohibited AI, AI literacy (both in force 2 Feb 2025) and transparency (2 Aug 2026). The word "just" drops AI literacy, which Farmer spells out at length. MISMATCH.

Bullet 2 says Juicebox added "auto-generated intake notes, aimed at speeding up healthcare role launches". Source says only "Healthcare recruiting data enrichment; intake notes so role launches can be easier" - no "auto-generated", and the healthcare scope applies to the data enrichment, not the intake notes. MISMATCH.

Bullet 3 says screening "now supports automatic disqualifying criteria". Source says "Application Screening now supports disqualifying criteria" - the word "automatic" is an addition not in the source. MISMATCH.

Bullet 3 says "OpenAI and Anthropic are in a credit dispute". The source describes a dispute between OpenAI and the two mathematicians, Tristan Buckmaster (NYU) and Levent Alpoge (who works at Anthropic). Nothing in the source makes Anthropic-the-company a party. Also "his own" understates a two-person team. MISMATCH.

Brief says Astra "pushes AI from chatting into actually operating your CRM and ATS". OpenAI's example tasks are "filling out online forms, updating customer records in a CRM" - no ATS. The library file itself states "neither source makes any explicit statement about labour-market or hiring-specific impact; that framing above is this newsletter's own read". The digest's own item bullet correctly says CRM only. MISMATCH.

Fix pass 1 after fact-check NOT CLEAR: dropped this item entirely from section 1 and the standout row. Library date is 2026-09-10, one day after the edition's 8-week window closes, and the newsletter's inference of "Wednesday 9 September" is not first-party evidence for re-dating the library record. Separately the guest surname is unverifiable: transcript auto-caption renders it "Kate", the description gives only "Cait", and a LinkedIn spelling is not publishable evidence. Not added to featured-log.tsv, so it stays eligible next week once its date sits inside the window.

With PromptMates Live/ElevenLabs dropped, refilled the Podcast standout slot per SELECTION.md section 6 from the remaining items. Chose Offer Accepted (Maggie Fish, Grafana Labs) over Recruiting Future and 10x Recruiting: it has the most concrete, triable tactic (the "guiding principles engine") plus a hard structural change (six interview stages to five), from a credible senior in-house voice. 10x Recruiting's contrarian take was close behind but less immediately actionable. Brainfood ineligible per SELECTION.md ("never Brainfood").

Fact-check found "I'm kind of a three" welds two separate phrases from 13:26 ("...this I'm kind of neutral on. So I I guess I'm a three."). Dropped the quotation marks and reworded to "stopped debriefs producing vague scores" rather than misquote.

during the low-rate years does not appear anywhere in the transcript; Yan says only "for various reasons", and the only period named ("the covid era") is the host's, not Yan's. Replaced the qualifier with Yan's actual wording, "for various reasons".

Bullet said "just the AI ban and the August transparency duty", omitting the AI literacy duty that Farmer discusses at length, also both dated 2 Feb 2025 not "this year". Rewrote to name all three live obligation sets (prohibited-AI ban, AI literacy, transparency) and dropped "just".

Bullet added "auto-generated" (not in source) and scoped intake notes to "healthcare role launches" when the source only scopes the data enrichment to healthcare, not the intake notes. Rewrote to match the source's own wording exactly.
Bullet added "automatic" before "disqualifying criteria", not supported by the source ("supports disqualifying criteria"). Cut the word.

Bullet said "OpenAI and Anthropic are in a credit dispute" and "his own breakthrough". Source describes a dispute between OpenAI and two mathematicians, Tristan Buckmaster (NYU) and Levent Alpoge (who happens to work at Anthropic), not the companies, and it was a two-person team. Rewrote to name the mathematicians correctly and drop "his own".
operating your CRM and ATS - OpenAI's own examples cover CRM only; the source file explicitly disclaims any hiring-specific claim. Cut "and ATS", brief now says CRM only, matching the item bullet.

Updated after fix pass 1: removed the dropped PromptMates Live/ElevenLabs item (12 items remain), updated the Offer Accepted/10x Recruiting/Brainfood/AI For Humans claim text to match the corrected digest wording, updated standout and brief cross-references to point at the new Podcast standout (Offer Accepted) and the CRM-only brief claim.

Round 2. Bullet 3 spells the mathematician's surname "Levent Alpoge". The library file renders it with an umlaut, "Alpoge" as A-l-p-U+00F6-g-e (hex 41 6c 70 c3 b6 67 65), in both the episode description and the summary block. The build has a plain o with no umlaut and no ö entity. Only surviving failure in the edition; a one-character fix, otherwise the bullet must be dropped (leaving a valid two-bullet item).

Round 2 fact-check: mathematician's surname was misspelled "Alpoge"; source (episode description and summary block) renders it "Alpöge", hex-verified 41 6c 70 c3 b6 67 65. Corrected as literal UTF-8 to match the file's existing convention (it already uses literal UTF-8 for ·, —, ', etc., no HTML entities for accented letters). Updated factcheck-input.json to match.

Round 3. Verified the Alpoge -> Alpoge-with-umlaut correction at byte level (41 6c 70 c3 b6 67 65, literal UTF-8, no entity); file decodes as strict UTF-8 with zero U+FFFD and no mojibake; full text re-extraction (146 lines) is identical to round 2 apart from that single character. All 10 round-1 findings and the 1 round-2 finding are resolved; no mismatches or unverifiable claims remain. Edition cleared to publish.

column4: JAMIE'S CALL, and a deliberate exception to SELECTION.md's never-go-backwards rule. That rule made TA Unboxed 2026-09-18 Part 1 permanently ineligible the moment Part 2 (09-22) was featured this week. The rule's own stated purpose is to stop a backfill slipping an OLDER item in a week AFTER a newer one from the same source, which reads as a mistake. Both halves of a two-parter inside the SAME edition is not that case, so the exception is sound rather than a rule being ignored. RECOMMEND writing it into SELECTION.md as a named carve-out: a multi-part series published inside one window may run together in one edition, ordered newest first, which is what was done here. Without that the rule keeps silently eating Part 1 of every two-parter.
